text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.48% today as oil prices stabilized following news of renewed U.S.-Iran peace efforts. Yesterday's sharp 2.8% drop (to $147.96) had been driven by that same geopolitical relief—markets feared lower crude prices if tensions eased and supply risks fell. Today's modest recovery suggests some of that selling exhausted itself, though crude prices remain volatile and elevated (U.S. oil at $103/barrel, significantly above normal ranges).

The broader move over two weeks—up 5.67%—reflects the energy sector's sensitivity to Middle East geopolitics. Oil majors like ConocoPhillips benefit from higher crude prices and the uncertainty that keeps them elevated; when peace talk hopes rise, that uncertainty shrinks and the stock tends to pull back. Trump's announced methane policy rollbacks, while positive for domestic production, are projected to have negligible effects on crude prices, so they're unlikely to be the driver here.
